Zychlin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żychlin, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Żychlin at the beginning of the 18th century; by 1921, 2,701 (39.5%) were mostly murdered in Chełmno in 1942. This cemetery, likely established in the mid-18th century alongside the kehilla, was described in a 1929 cemetery list as 'fenced, in good condition.' During WWII, it became an execution site: about 160 Jews shot in March 1942, and another 200 forced laborers murdered that fall. Germans and local residents alike stole matzevot for construction; the grounds later served as pasture. Poland's local council voted for closure on September 25, 1965, formalized by the Minister of Municipal Economy on March 22, 1966. In 1992, Mosze Zyslender funded lapidaries from recovered tombstone fragments and a Holocaust victims' monument; more recently, Izrael Meir Gabaj commissioned a commemorative tombstone for tzadik Szmuel Aba from Żychlin (d. 1879).
